01Rationale

Why this level matters

One person with AI can now do work that once needed a team, which lowers the cost of starting and raises the standard for what you offer. This course covers the fundamentals of building a business and a consulting practice, with AI as part of how you work.

02Target competencies

Intended learning outcomes

Shape an offer

Define who you serve, what problem you solve and why you.

Win customers

Sell and negotiate with confidence and a clear process.

Plan the business

Write a business plan with numbers you can defend.

Run lean with AI

Use AI to do more with a small team, and know its limits.

03Planned scope

Proposed scope: 16 lessons in 4 modules

This outline describes the intended curriculum. Lesson materials and assessments are not yet available.

Module 1Starting

From idea to offer.

  1. Finding a problem worth solving
  2. Starting and scaling a business
  3. Freelancing and consulting
  4. Pricing and positioning

Module 2Selling

Win and keep customers.

  1. Sales conversations
  2. Negotiation
  3. Proposals and contracts
  4. Customer relationships

Module 3Planning

Put it in numbers.

  1. Business plan development
  2. Finances and cash flow
  3. E-commerce and digital products
  4. Legal and tax basics

Module 4Working with AI

One person, more reach.

  1. AI in your daily work
  2. Automating the routine
  3. Where AI should not decide
  4. Your 90-day plan

04Planned practical work

Your offer and business plan

Proposed project: Build your offer, business plan and pitch for a business or consulting practice you could start. This practical component will be developed and validated before the level opens.

The steps

  1. Define the customer and the problem
  2. Write the offer and the price
  3. Write the sales process
  4. Build the financial plan
  5. Plan the first ninety days
  6. Write and practise the pitch

Intended validation criteria

  • The offer names a specific customer and problem
  • The financial plan states its assumptions
  • The pitch fits in three minutes

05How you learn

Proposed learning design

Worked examples

The professional academies begin with complete examples and make the reasoning behind good decisions visible.

Guided practice

Scaffolds fade as learners progress—from annotated examples to structured tasks and independent work.

Retrieval and review

Low-stakes questions prompt recall; review revisits important concepts. Model answers and rubrics make improvement specific.

Research-informed updates

The academies cite primary research and standards, record review dates and receive versioned updates as evidence changes.

The proposed learning design draws on retrieval practice, worked examples and spaced review; detailed learner materials will be published before release. Read the evidence and sources.

06Intended audience

What you need

No experience needed. An idea you want to test is helpful.
